links.outcome: Stand-alone AI lesion-level accuracy by patient sex, age, and rib side
links.effect: AI accuracy was 81.6% in males vs 63.0% in females (p<0.001). Accuracy was lower with increasing age (true 63.54 vs false 69.40 years, p<0.001). Accuracy was higher for left- than right-sided fractures (72.5% vs 65.6%, p=0.029).
links.quote: Age did not impact the radiologists’ diagnostic accuracy (p = 0.802); however, AI showed a decrease in accuracy with increasing patient age (p < 0.001) ( Fig 4 and Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Patient-level diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of AI-assisted radiologists versus standard double-reading
links.effect: AI-assisted sensitivity was 94.2% versus 69.2% for double-reading: increase 25.0% (95% CI: 10.5, 39.5; P < 0.001). Specificity was 100% versus 98.2%.
links.quote: The sensitivity at patient level was estimated at 94.2% in AI-assisted group and 69.2% in double-reading, with an increase estimated at 25.0% (95% CI: 10.5, 39.5; P < 0.001).
